question: The interest accrued on a sum of ₹16,000 lent at a simple interest rate of 14% p.a. for the time in those many years, which gives a simple interest of three-fifths of a certain sum at 10% p.a., is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time (T) = (SI fraction × 100) ÷ Rate

T = (3/5 × 100) ÷ 10 = 6 years.

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

SI = (16000 × 14 × 6) ÷ 100 = 13440

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,440.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI₁) = 3/5 of Sum (P₁)

Rate (R₁) = 10% p.a.

New Principal (P₂) = ₹16,000

New Rate (R₂) = 14% p.a.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Step 1: Find Time (T)
 SI = 3/5 × Sum
 Rate = 10% p.a.
 T = (3 × 100) ÷ (5 × 10) = 6 yrs

 
• 
 

 
 Step 2: Find Interest
 P = ₹16,000
 R = 14% p.a., T = 6 yrs
 SI = P × R × T ÷ 100

 
 Final Interest = ₹13,440

**Calculations:**

Let the required time be T years.

⇒ SI₁ = (P₁ × R₁ × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 × P₁ = (P₁ × 10 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = T ÷ 10

⇒ T = (3 × 10) ÷ 5 = 6 years

Now, calculate the simple interest (SI₂) on ₹16,000 for 6 years at 14% p.a.

⇒ SI₂ = (16000 × 14 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 160 × 84

⇒ SI₂ = 13440

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,440.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated uniformly on the original principal amount. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount A at the end of the given time period is the sum of the initial principal and the generated simple interest. Formula: A = P + SI = P × (1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

Finding Principal from Interest

When the simple interest generated over a period is known, the principal can be calculated by rearranging the standard formula as: P = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T).
